If you are taking cetirizine for hives, get emergency medical help immediately if you have trouble swallowing, dizziness, swelling of the tongue or around the mouth, trouble speaking, drooling, or wheezing. Cetirizine is not a substitute for an epinephrine injector. Do not use cetirizine to prevent hives from known causes such as foods, insect stings, or medicines. Call your doctor if your hives do not improve after 3 days, if they last more than 6 weeks, or if they are an unusual color, look bruised or blistered, or do not itch.

qualifiers.risk: increased dizziness, drowsiness and difficulty concentrating

triples.evidence_text: Q: Can you take Benadryl and cetirizine together? A: Benadryl should not be taken at the same time as cetirizine because it can increase side effects such as dizziness, drowsiness, and difficulty concentrating. Some people, especially the elderly or children, may also find their thinking, judgement, and coordination impaired. You should also not drink alcohol while taking either of these medications because it can make these side effects worse.

qualifiers.formulation: cetirizine alone, not a combination with pseudoephedrine

triples.evidence_text: Q: Can cetirizine raise blood pressure? A: Cetirizine does not increase blood pressure and blood pressure is not listed as a side effect in the product information. But cetirizine can be found in combination with other medications, such as pseudoephedrine in products such as Zyrtec-D, and pseudoephedrine does increase blood pressure.

Q: How long does it take for cetirizine to work? A: Cetirizine is an allergy medicine that usually starts to work within about 20 to 60 minutes after you take it. Many people notice less sneezing and itching within the first hour, especially if they take it on an empty stomach. One dose of cetirizine generally provides relief for up to 24 hours, so most people only need to take it once a day.
